Anya (PM): Heads-up from field: three enterprise customers want model pins with multi-month TTLs to avoid migration churn. They asked for 'no surprise' behavior.
Carlos (Field SE): Yep. They want to lock a specific model version for the duration of the contract. Main ask is predictability, not cost.
Mei (Solutions): Idea: a configurable TTL pin resource + "gracepin" semantics. Gracepin = pinned until TTL expires unless a quality/regression trigger fires. Customers get alerts before any manual migration.
Ravi (Eng Lead): We can do that but need clear launch gates. Proposal: (A) tenant-provided benchmark artifacts pass our perf/quality checks; (B) staged canary at ~10% traffic for 48h with monitoring; (C) runbook + rollback automation.
Joan (ProdOps): Operational constraints: pinned older model may have different latency/cost. We need to capture SLA impact in the pin contract and a comms template for CS/AE.
Legal (Counsel): Legal wants an opt-in clause for pin exceptions and explicit cap on TTL in SOW. Also want language about risks if vendor discontinues a model.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Benchmark thresholds suggestion: 95th pct latency <= 120% of tenant baseline; p50/p90 within 110%; token throughput unchanged. Quality: eval on 3 tenant prompt cohorts, aggregate delta <= 2% for key metrics (F1/QA/semantic-similarity depending on task).
Anya (PM): Add a "pin-health" composite signal made of latency-delta, error-rate, and quality-delta. If any submetric exceeds threshold, pin enters "hold" state and notifies product + field.
pin-bot: pin-health webhook registered -> posts to #eng-oncall and #product when state changes (dev-hours only by default).
Mei (Solutions): Request flow: Field files a Pin Request with tenant artifact (CSV/test prompts), desired TTL parameter, and business rationale. Infra runs auto-checks and returns a pass/fail + diagnostics. Product signs off on pass -> infra issues pin resource. Manual unpin allowed with exec approval or emergency rollback.
Carlos (Field SE): Can TTL be per-tenant? Yes, some customers need 3 months, others 12.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Implementation guardrails: default max TTL = 6 months; >6 months requires VP product approval; absolute cap 12 months. Also expire pins with automatic notification 30 days and 7 days before TTL end.
Joan (ProdOps): I'll draft SOW clause options (3m/6m/12m) + a one-pager for AMs showing expected operational tradeoffs.
Legal (Counsel): I'll template the contract language around pin liability, deprecation escapes, and customer opt-in for >6 months.
Anya (PM): Launch checklist (minimum): 1) pin-health metrics spec; 2) infra auto-validation prototype; 3) canary orchestration runbook; 4) SOW + comms; 5) legal signoff for template clauses.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Technical action: I'll produce a metrics spec doc (latency histograms, error categories, evaluation harness) and a minimal infra prototype that can validate a CSV within 48h. ETA: EOD Wed.
Mei (Solutions): I'll build a request form prototype (internal UI + API) and example benchmark CSV. ETA: Fri EOD.
Joan (ProdOps): I'll share SOW and comms drafts by Monday.
Carlos (Field SE): Field will collect initial tenant artifacts and arrange customer readouts.
Anya (PM): Decision on TTL caps: we default to max 6 months; exceptions flagged for exec approval. If everyone agrees I'll log this to the product roadmap and inform sales.
Ravi (Eng Lead): Agree. Also we should add automated nightly checks for pinned models to catch silent regressions.
Anya (PM): Good call. Owners recap: Ravi = metrics + infra prototype, Mei = request flow, Joan = SOW/comms, Legal = contract language, Carlos = customer artifacts. I'll follow up with a short implementation RFC. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
